item.title: More than 100 vendors will bring decades of vintage fashion to Oaks
item.description: More than 100 vendors will gather for the 18th edition of The Philly Vintage Flea on Sunday, March 29, from noon to 5 p.m. at the Greater Philadelphia Expo Center.

item.title: Former treasurer at Plymouth Meeting nonprofit allegedly stole $246,000 to pay for vacations, hot tub
item.description: Montgomery County prosecutors have charged Michael Fantuzzo, 40, with stealing $246,000 from the Pennsylvania Occupational Therapy Association while he served as treasurer. He allegedly used the money to pay for vacations and a hot tub.

item.title: To find homes for some of PSPCA's oldest pets, Ensemble Arts is offering free tickets to 'Beauty and the Beast'
item.description: Ensemble Arts Philly is giving away free 'Beauty and the Beast' tickets to anyone who adopts one of eight pets that the Pennsylvania SPCA says are among its oldest and most overlooked animals. Adoption fees also are being waived.

item.title: Pennie enrollment plummets as health insurance premiums increase by 102%
item.description: Pennie enrollment decreased in 2026 after plan costs increased by an average of 102%. The state marketplace attributed ACA health insurance price hikes to expired enhanced federal tax credits.

item.title: Montgomery County man arrested for alleged role in Nigerian scam
item.description: A Montgomery County man has been arrested and indicted for allegedly helping Nigerian scammers launder stolen money. Samuel D. Marcus, 33, received wire transfers and converted funds into cryptocurrency, prosecutors say.

item.title: What to know about the Universal Theme Parks exhibition opening at The Franklin Institute
item.description: “Universal Theme Parks: The Exhibition” opens at The Franklin Institute on Feb. 14, 2026, for its world premiere. The show runs through Sept. 7 in the Nicholas and Athena Karabots Pavilion and Mandell Center.

item.title: A brain game may cut risk of Alzheimer's disease by 25%, study finds
item.description: Some older adults who complete specific cognitive exercises, called speed training, may lower their risk of developing dementia by 25%, new research shows. It's the first 'clear documentation' that cognitive training may lower the risk of Alzheimer's disease, one expert says.

item.title: Instant observations: Short-handed Sixers shrink vs. red-hot Trail Blazers
item.description: All things considered, the Sixers will take a 3-2 road trip. But a loss punctuated by another catastrophic third quarter was not the way the Sixers wanted their Western Conference swing to end.
